rows.chat: ma / tenze3jesh min ay ishi taani
rows.why: He dropped the you-form t again after her 23:04 fix (framed as 'there's no ma, right?'); Amal: 'La, it doesn't work. تنزعجش'.
The drill was the -ish negative; he gave plain ma + verb without -sh; Amal: 'No. Where's your ish?'
rows.proposed_rule: Negative with -ish: add -sh to the end of the verb (bahkeesh, ma tenbestish fiyyo zyaade); a command keeps its t- (tenze3jesh).

A number said alone (65 degrees, no counted noun after it) keeps the -e: 5amse u sitteen. Amal 'No' (08:10) and 'مش خمس' (08:13); at 06:35 she had just asked when the أ/-e is dropped and he said 'when we're counting'. This is a new slip 2 minutes after A6, not a repeat.

He repeated her example الدروس صعبة 5 s later with a different word; in a lesson about feminine adjectives for non-human plurals, السبع is the engine's spelling of el-sa3b (masculine, with el-), not 'the seven'. Amal 'No. صعبة.' and he answered 'Oh, you're saying the singular feminine' - he took her fix. Speaking (him saying the rule's form), not a listening misread.

held_one_reader.proposed_rule: Negating a verb in spoken Levantine adds -ish at the end as well as ma in front: ma tenbestish fiyyo (don't enjoy it), ma tenze3jesh.
